POS North Star · Discovery Draft

Transactions & Settlement

An audit of the current Transactions section, what the older iteration got right, and the proposal for a north-star direction. Scoped to one persona: merchants for whom Transactions and Settlement are the highest-value screens on the app.

What we're auditing

Persona
Merchants with high batch throughput. Settlement and reconciliation are daily. Kirana / low-volume out of scope.
Terminology
Only what the current Figma actually shows — TID, RRN, POS ID, Batch No., Batch Status.

12 findings, pinned onto the real screens. Grouped by the aspect of the experience they touch.

Transactions list

Frame 37:5531 · Today · SQR + non-SQR mix

1
F-T01The screen carries a period switcher ("Today"), a filter, a search, tabs, and a Settle CTA — four jobs at once. For this persona it should default to the reconciliation job (the current open batch), not a flat live feed.
2
F-T04Search behind an icon. No visible search field on the list header. Merchants hunting for a specific TID have to know the icon exists.
3
F-T07"Settle Batch" as a header CTA with no summary of what's about to settle — the biggest gap for this persona. Fixed in the Proposal.
4
F-T02Rows show time only, no date. Day-close reconciliation needs the date on every row.
5
F-T03Status vocabulary leaks — Success, Failed, Pending here, plus Voided, Cancelled, REFUNDED-initiated elsewhere. Six values, three casing conventions.
Two more list variants worth calling out

Static QR-specific view (right, frame 37:5531) — same list, but header explains "All SQR Transactions done in the Store for the last 3 days are listed in the order of recency". The 3-day copy line proves the list already spans multiple days — which makes hiding the date on the row (finding 4 above) a bug, not a decision. Non-SQR variant replaces the SQR tab with a full-width "Settle Batch" — different composition, same missing preview.

List composition varies by config

Frames 37:5531 (SQR) · 37:4570 (non-SQR)

The persona sees at least three different Transactions surfaces depending on their configuration. Whether or not the batch-summary treatment we're proposing gets applied to each of them consistently is the unlock — right now they diverge on the header without any pattern.

Detail card — Success (UPI & Card)

Frames 37:5717 · 37:6306

1
F-T08Batch Status: Open on every detail card — always Open, never anything else. The proposal treats settled/open as a property of the batch (not the transaction) and replaces this field with a link to the parent Batch.
2
F-T12Nine to eleven data rows, all styled the same weight. Anchor rows for this persona are Amount + TID + Batch — the rest is lookup data. Hierarchy should say that.
3
Batch No. exists (284) but it's a passive text row with no affordance. In the proposal this becomes a tappable link to the Batch Detail screen.
4
UPI success shows just Home + Reprint. No Void action — void only appears on card transactions (right). Consistent: card is voidable pre-settle, UPI reversal is different mechanically.
5
Void is in the bottom nav on card transactions. Good discoverability, but the surface is small and Void is destructive — worth reviewing whether it needs a top-of-detail placement + confirmation, not a tab-bar-adjacent item.

Detail card — Failure

Frame 37:7031 · Host decline

1
"Could not connect to the acquirer host" — clear error. Good.
2
F-T10"In case customer is debited, amount to be refunded to customer" — the copy names the responsibility but the screen offers no action to fulfil it. The merchant is told they own the problem and given no tool to solve it.
3
Bottom nav collapses to just Home. No Retry, no Refund, no Escalate. If this is a mundane, retry-able event, retry should be inline. If it needs refund, refund should be one tap.

How Razorpay and Paytm handle the same job

Device captures of the live Razorpay POS and Paytm All-in-One POS apps. Different design languages, but the mental-model choices are what matter — both work with real merchant data.

Headline finding

Neither Razorpay nor Paytm has a batch object. Both use "the day" as the unit of work. Pine Labs is the only one of the three with an explicit batch — which is either a real advantage (batches are how acquiring works, and enterprise merchants track them) or an over-engineered concept we're carrying without payoff. The proposal doubles down on it; this tab helps decide whether that's right.

Razorpay — payment detail

Two levels · summary + reconciliation deep-dive

13
Anchor block: green tick + ₹1 + "Payment Settled". Status is on the money moment, not on a batch relationship. Same anchoring pattern we proposed for Pine Labs' rewrite.
14
Print Receipt as the primary action — one big touch target. Not tucked into a bottom nav row.

Paytm — Payment History

Date-scoped list · header KPI tiles

17
"Print History" as a top-right button. Export is a first-class action, always visible. Pine Labs has no equivalent.
18
Four filter facets (Date · Status · Card Machine · Payment Source), each a chip-dropdown. More facets than Razorpay's three or Pine Labs' two — including Card Machine (relevant only when a merchant has multiple terminals).
19
Header KPI tiles: "Successful Payments 5 · Payment Received ₹48,435.76". Inline on the list, not a separate dashboard screen. This is exactly the pattern our proposal put on Transactions as the batch header — just day-scoped.
20
21

Paytm — filter sheets

Bottom sheet per facet · flat list of options

20
Cancel / Refund is one combined status. The opposite call from Razorpay, and cleaner than Pine Labs' three-way split (Voided / cancelled / REFUNDED initiated). Which one's right depends on whether your persona needs to distinguish these operationally — for our high-batch persona, they're different events, so we're going with Razorpay's split.
21
Payment Source filters by the payer's rail (Credit / Debit / UPI / Wallet / Postpaid Loan / Paytm Payments Bank). A payer-side facet — Pine Labs' filter mixes payer rails with issuers, Paytm doesn't.

What this means for our proposal

Direct validations
  • F-T09 (Void/Refund split) — Razorpay does exactly what we're proposing: two separate status pills, distinct terminal states. Not just our call — the market call.
  • Batch Detail component (Proposal Q2/Q4) — Razorpay's My Dashboard is the same pattern (KPI + mode-wise breakdown), just day-scoped. Our version at batch scope is a straight generalisation.
  • Header KPIs on the list (proposed Transactions header) — Paytm already does this at day scope. We're doing it at batch scope. Zero learning cost for merchants coming from either competitor.
  • F-T02 (no date on row) — Both competitors fix it with a date-grouped header. Cheaper than adding a date field to every row.
Genuine differentiator to defend

The batch object is unique to us. Razorpay and Paytm both use the day. The question the proposal has to answer: does batch matter operationally for enterprise / high-throughput merchants — the persona this doc is scoped to? If yes, we lead with it. If it's a legacy concept from the acquiring stack, we should consider dropping it and matching the day-scoped model.

Ideas worth stealing
  • Razorpay: "Settled" as a distinct pill from "Success" · date-grouped headers · icon-tile filter grid · Print Receipt as primary action on detail · Device Details grouping on the detail (fixes F-T12).
  • Paytm: "Print History" as a top-level action on the list · KPI tiles as a persistent header · Card Machine as a filter facet (relevant when merchant has multiple terminals) · Payment Source facet with a clean flat taxonomy.

Mental model

One-liner

The batch is the unit of work. The day is a sequence of batches.

Home has "two doors, one status light" (Collect / Show QR / status). Transactions has this. Every design decision on Transactions and Settlement should answer to it: is this thing a property of the batch, or a property of a single transaction? Put it where its unit-of-work says it belongs.

The four proposed screens

Same visual language as the existing app. Four screens make the batch a first-class object without breaking anything already built.

Batch Detail core

One component. Rendered at three fidelities.

KPI tiles, mode-wise breakdown, adjustments (voids/refunds), net after adjustments. The Settle CTA lives here, not on the list — the merchant sees exactly what they're settling before they fire it.

Post-settle the same screen renders with the Settled pill, a Close time, receipt CTAs (Print / Share), and no Settle button.

Home renders a compact tile version of the same data — one line: "Open batch · ₹X · N txns · Settle".

Transaction Detail — rewritten fix

Replaces frame 37:5717 / 37:6306

Anchor block: Amount + status + TID. The three things that carry the reconciliation weight, sized to say so.

Batch link replaces the passive "Batch No. 117 · Batch Status: Open" pair. One tap → Batch Detail. F-T08 killed cleanly.

Reference info collapses — RRN, POS ID, Transaction Type live behind a disclosure for dispute research, not on the front page.

Void becomes a first-class action on the detail (not a nav-bar item), with distinct styling to signal destructiveness. Refund would appear here instead of Void for settled transactions — same slot, different action.

What each proposal call does

1 · Default Transactions to batch-scoped suggestion

Instead of a chronological feed of the last few days, the list opens scoped to the current open batch. All batches is one tap away for historical work. This is the "current batch is your live workspace, past batches are your archive" split.

2 · One batch-summary component, three placements view

The Batch Detail screen above is the summary. Same component renders at three fidelities: full-screen on Batch Detail, header-strip on Transactions, one-line tile on Home. Authored once, three surfaces inherit it.

3 · Void and Refund remain distinct decided

Void = current-batch transaction, pre-settlement, reversed at source. Refund = settled transaction, post-batch-close, new outbound. Both are first-class actions on the detail with distinct copy and distinct terminal states. The detail card slot for the primary action just swaps between them based on whether the parent batch is Open or Settled.

4 · Batch is a first-class object core

All Batches list. Batch Detail screen. Batch link on the transaction card. Three moves, one mental model. Settled/open lives on the batch, not smuggled onto every transaction row.

What comes next

  • Sanity-check with PM and engineering on the batch data model — the frames assume Batch #N is a queryable object with count, mode-wise totals, and open/settled timestamps. Confirm.
  • Screenshots of Settlement pre/post and the Void modal from the current file — pinned in the Audit tab to complete the pre-image side.
  • Competitor sweep — Razorpay and Paytm Transactions/Settlement, same lens.
  • Post-settle and failure-state variants of Batch Detail — same component, different state.

Frameworks used

Same 14-framework lens as the Home audit.

Cognition & motor
Hick's Law
Decision time grows with number of choices. Filter sheets and status vocabularies bear the load.
Fitts's Law
Time to acquire a target depends on its size and distance. Applies to Settle Batch, Void, and the search affordance.
Miller's 7±2
Short-term memory limits. Detail cards with nine to eleven undifferentiated rows overflow this.
Learnability & consistency
Jakob's Law
Users expect this app to work like others. Reconciliation surfaces, filter patterns, receipt actions.
Nielsen's 10 Heuristics
Visibility of status, match to real world, user control, consistency, error prevention.
Shneiderman's 8 Rules
Strive for consistency, meaningful feedback, dialogs to closure — Settle Batch fails all three.
Gerhardt-Powals
Reduce uncertainty; group data meaningfully; present new information with meaningful aids.
Perception & form
Gestalt Principles
Similarity, proximity, common region. How the filter groups fail similarity.
Norman's Design
Affordances, signifiers, feedback, constraints. Void as an action that needs a signifier.
Tognazzini's Principles
Interface should look and behave the same across screens. Detail card variants fail this.
Behaviour & trust
Fogg Behavior Model
Behaviour = motivation × ability × prompt. Settle Batch has the first two; the design has removed confidence.
Cialdini's Influence
Commitment / consistency, authority. Confirmations and receipt copy are trust-carriers.
Peak-End Rule
Users remember peaks and ends of an experience. Settle-success and Void-processing are peak/end moments.
Content & access
10 Content Design Heuristics
Clear, concise, consistent, inclusive, plain-language. Status vocabulary and error copy get audited here.
WCAG 2.1 AA
Contrast, target size, keyboard access. Applies especially to status pill colour + label combinations.
